limitations: Relevance to published articles is not acceptance probability, editorial judgment, manuscript quality or a guarantee of journal eligibility.
Published-paper labels encode publication and selection bias; rejected and transferred submissions are unavailable.
The observed publishing journal is only one label. Other journals can be appropriate; top-k recovery is not complete relevance assessment.
English, abstract-bearing indexed papers are an incomplete and uneven source sample; uncovered journals cannot receive corpus-based recommendations.
Per-journal forward splits are temporal within each journal, not a single global as-of backtest; other journals may have later training dates.
Frozen MiniLM embeddings are not biomedical fine-tuning. A transformer was not trained on this corpus.
The independent evaluator splits the raw corpus before rights filtering, quarantining excess same-day boundary ties. Sparse journals and indexing delays remain temporal-evaluation limitations.
Manuscripts and embeddings are processed on device by the browser integration. This model core does not transmit or persist queries.

Article-level vectors may disclose source information. Only records with documented CC BY, CC0 or public-domain rights enter fitting, validation selection and public export; the broader raw temporal test remains private.
Abstention uses lower-tail known-paper validation similarities. Without external negatives its out-of-domain sensitivity is unknown.
rightsPolicy: CC BY, CC0 or public domain with article-specific license evidence and checked date; unknown/NC/ND/SA excluded.
